name: WiFiAware
summary: Securely pair and connect to external devices over peer-to-peer Wi-Fi.

declarations.name: WAAccessCategory
declarations.comment:
The underling quality-of-service (QoS) the Wi-Fi layer uses to transmit data packets from a connection over the air.

A given `NetworkConnection` is bound to a single access category at the Wi-Fi layer, based on the configuration of `NWParameter`'s  `serviceClass` property.
This allows your app to specify how the Wi-Fi layer transmits the `NetworkConnection`'s data packets, selecting the performance characteristics that are relevant to the data flow.

Wi-Fi is a shared medium, so all Wi-Fi devices, networks, apps, and  `NetworkConnection`s share the overall Wi-Fi capacity between them. An app can improve the performance of its data flows, and that of all other nearby devices and Wi-Fi networks, by choosing the lowest QoS category that meets the requirements of each of its flows.
When in doubt, use the default `.bestEffort` category.

For more information, refer to [NWParameters.ServiceClass](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/network/nwparameters/serviceclass-swift.enum) and [NWParameters](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/network/nwparameters).

Access categories are typically created by the system on behalf of the client, so they usually don't need to be instantiated directly.

declarations.comment: A structure that checks the host device's supported features and capabilities.

members.name: supportedFeatures
members.comment:
A property that returns a set of supported features, or an empty set if the current platform doesn't support Wi-Fi Aware.

If the host device doesn't support Wi-Fi Aware, the system returns an empty set. If a
feature is present in the set, it's supported, which you can test by using the code below:

```swift
let isSupported = WACapabilities.supportedFeatures.contains(feature)
```

declarations.name: WAPairedDevice
declarations.comment:
A known Wi-Fi Aware device that your app can connect to.

Your app may request the system securely pair and grant access to remote devices. Use
[AccessorySetupKit](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/accessorysetupkit/) or
[DeviceDiscoveryUI](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/devicediscoveryui)
to add the devices to the set of `WAPairedDevice.Devices` that your app may connect to on-demand.
The list of paired devices can change over time as a person adds and removes devices from the system.

members.name: allDevices
allDevices
description
members.comment: A string description of the publisher.

members.name: pairingInfo
members.comment:
The unauthenticated information provided by the device before a person pairs it for the first time.

The value is `nil` if the information is unavailable. The values provide a capture of what the system receives prior to the first pairing the device, and don't reflect any information received post-pairing. If your app needs more up-to-date info, query the device via the secure Wi-Fi Aware data path.

- Warning: Don't use these values for any purpose other than to assist a person during the initial one-time pairing process.
Because the system receives the values before the initial pairing, they're transmitted over an insecure, unauthenticated, and unencrypted channel. Consequently, they may be intercepted or manipulated by an attacker, making it impossible to verify their accuracy.
Therefore, if your app requires reliable and detailed information about the connected device, it needs to obtain it through the secure Wi-Fi Aware data path after pairing is complete, rather than relying on the content in this structure.

members.name: id
members.comment:
A stable ID that you can use to uniquely identify a device.

The ID is stable for the lifetime of a single app install on a single device. This value is the same as the value provided in
[AccessorySetupKit](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/accessorysetupkit/)'s `ASAccessory/wifiAwarePairedDeviceID`.

members.name: name
members.comment: The user-provided name of the device as a string, or `nil` if not available.

declarations.name: WAPairedDevice.Devices
declarations.comment:
A dictionary holding a snapshot of currently paired devices accessible and known to your app.

An empty dictionary indicates that no paired devices are known to your app.

declarations.name: WAPairedDevice.DevicesSequence
declarations.comment:
A sequence that vends updates to a paired device list, as the list changes.

The `DevicesSequence` produces an asynchronous sequence of
``WAPairedDevice/Devices`` items, providing the latest snapshot of the
paired devices known to your app.

members.name: makeAsyncIterator
members.comment:
Makes an asynchronous iterator that provides successive device snapshots when the list of paired devices known to the app changes.
- Returns: A new asynchronous iterator vending ``WAPairedDevice/Devices`` elements when changes occur.

members.name: current
members.comment:
Fetches a one-time snapshot of all paired devices that are currently known and  accessible to your app.

The ``WAPairedDevice/Devices`` dictionary holds a snapshot of the currently paired devices that are known and accessible to your app.
This method returns an empty dictionary if there are no paired devices known to your app.
The following code is an example of how to use `current()` to return the first `Devices` snapshot in the sequence:

```swift
guard let devices = try await WAPairedDevice.allDevices.current() { return }
```

Don't use this method if you need to monitor for changes to the paired device list, or change app behavior in
response to such changes. Instead, use

```swift
for try await devices in WAPairedDevice.allDevices {
	// Process the devices.
}
```

- Returns: A single ``WAPairedDevice/Devices`` element holding a snapshot of the currently paired devices known to the app, or `nil` if the sequence has no more values.
> Throws: An error if the system can't read the sequence, or if the app isn't permitted to access Wi-Fi Aware devices.
- seeAlso: ``WAPairedDevice/allDevices``
- seeAlso: ``WAPairedDevice/allDevices(matching:)``

Returns the next dictionary in the sequence.

The ``WAPairedDevice/Devices`` dictionary holds the latest snapshot of the currently paired devices that are known and accessible to your app.

- Returns: The next ``WAPairedDevice/Devices`` snapshot, or `nil` if it's at the end of the sequence.
> Throws: An error if the system can't read the sequence, or if your app isn't permitted to access Wi-Fi Aware devices.

declarations.name: WAPairedDevice.PairingInfo
declarations.comment:
A collection of unauthenticated information the system receives from a device before it's paired for the first time.

For privacy reasons, these values are only sent during initial pairing over Wi-Fi Aware, with a:
- **`Publisher`**: Include it in publish frames when you enable Wi-Fi Aware pair setup.
- **`Subscriber`**: Include it in the pairing bootstrap request frame when you pair to a publisher.

After initial pairing completes, the system no longer sends these values in any over-the-air frames, to prevent user tracking and protect user privacy.

> Warning: These values are only intended to assist a person during the initial one-time pairing process and shouldn't be used for any other purpose.
Because the system receives the values before the initial pairing, the system transmits them over an insecure, unauthenticated, and unencrypted channel. Consequently, they may be intercepted or manipulated by an attacker, making it impossible to verify their accuracy.
Therefore, if your app requires reliable and detailed information about the connected device, it should obtain it through the secure Wi-Fi Aware data path after pairing is complete, rather than relying on the content in this structure.

members.name: vendorName
members.comment:
The human-readable name of the manufacturer or vendor of the physical device as a person would understand it.

The system receives this data from the device within an DNS-SD TXT record. The value set in the `vendorName` property is the  value that follows the DNS-SD TXT record key:
```
vendorName=
```
The system interprets the value as an <= 63-byte UTF-8 string and may truncate it if it's longer than 63 bytes. Refer to
[RFC 6763](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6763#section-6.3) for more information on the over-the-air encoding.

members.name: description
members.comment: A string description of the pairing information.

members.name: pairingName
members.comment:
The human-readable name of the physical device as a person sees it during initial pairing.

The system receives this data from the device within an DNS-SD TXT record. The value set in the `pairingName` property is the  value that follows the DNS-SD TXT record key:
```
pairingName=
```
The system interprets the value as an <= 63-byte UTF-8 string and may truncate it if it's longer than 63 bytes. Refer to
[RFC 6763](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6763#section-6.3) for more information on the over-the-air encoding.

members.name: modelName
members.comment:
The human-readable model name of the physical device as a person can understand it.

The system receives this data from the device within an DNS-SD TXT record. The value set in the `modelName` property is the  value that follows the DNS-SD TXT record key:
```
modelName=
```
The system interprets the value as an <= 63-byte UTF-8 string and may truncate it if it's longer than 63 bytes. Refer to [RFC 6763](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6763#section-6.3) for more information on the over-the-air encoding

declarations.name: WAParameters
declarations.comment:
Parameters configuring a Wi-Fi Aware data path connection.

You can customize Wi-Fi Aware configuration with the parameters passed in the
`.wifiAware()` instruction to the `NetworkBrowser` and
`NetworkListener`, or via the `.wifiAware:WAParameters?` property on
`NWParameters`.

For more information about creating a `NetworkListener`, refer to ``WAPublisherListener/DatapathParameters``

> Important: Each service must have the same ``WAPerformanceMode`` on both the `NetworkBrowser` (subscriber) and `NetworkListener` (publisher) sides of the connection, or the resulting performance behavior is undefined. If not specified, the performance mode defaults to ``WAPerformanceMode/bulk`` on both sides.

members.name: performanceMode
members.comment: The initial performance configuration of the data path when connected.

members.comment: The initial performance configuration of the data path when connected.

members.comment: Initializes the parameters with defaults.

members.name: defaults
members.comment:
The property that configures default parameters that prioritize bulk throughput, power consumption, and other concurrent Wi-Fi use cases.

- Returns: Default parameters.

members.name: realtime
members.comment:
The property that configures parameters that prioritize latency at the expense of throughput, power consumption, and other concurrent Wi-Fi use cases.

- Returns: Realtime parameters.

declarations.name: WAPath

declarations.name: WAPerformanceForecast
declarations.comment: The performance forecast for a connection setup to the remote device.

members.name: localTimestamp
members.comment: The time the forecast was generated, using a local monotonically increasing clock.

members.name: signalStrength
members.comment:
The estimated signal strength of the remote device.

The resulting value can be between `0.0` (weakest) and `1.0` (strongest), or it can be `nil` if the system can't measure the value.

members.name: localThroughputCeiling
members.comment:
The highest throughput a connection from the local device to the remote device is capable of under ideal conditions, given the hardware capabilities of the local device.
The actual throughput achieved can be lower in the presence of other active connections.

The result is in `Mbps` and can be `nil` if the system can't calculate it.

members.name: localThroughputCapacity
members.comment:
The estimated average throughput capacity of the local device for a connection setup to the remote device.

The result is in `Mbps` and can be `nil` if the system can't calculate the capacity.

members.name: localThroughputCapacityRatio
members.comment:
The estimated normalized ratio of the local throughput capacity and the local throughput ceiling.

This ratio reflects the estimated throughput capability for a connection setup to the remote device as a value between `0.0` and `1.0`.

members.name: unavailabilityLatencyCeiling
members.comment:
The highest forecasted packet latency due to this device's unavailability.

This only considers the latency caused by time periods where this local device is not able to communicate to the other device via Wi-Fi Aware.
Additional latency can be caused by channel or RF conditions.

members.name: localInfrastructureThroughputCapacityRatio
members.comment:
The estimated normalized ratio of the local Wi-Fi Infrastructure throughput capacity and the local Wi-Fi Infrastructure throughput ceiling, if a Wi-Fi Aware connection is setup to the remote device.

This ratio reflects the estimated throughput capability for a connection setup to the remote device as a value between `0.0` and `1.0`.

members.name: timestamp
members.comment: The time the forecast was generated.

declarations.name: WAPerformanceMode
declarations.comment:
The performance mode that indicates what performance criterion to prioritize.

> Important: Each service must have the same ``WAPerformanceMode`` on both the
`NetworkBrowser` (subscriber) and `NetworkListener` (publisher) sides of the
connection, or the performance behavior is undefined. If not specified, the performance
mode defaults to ``bulk`` on both sides.

declarations.name: WAPerformanceReport
declarations.comment: The current performance state of the data path.

members.name: localTimestamp
members.comment: The time the report was generated, using a local monotonically increasing clock.

members.name: signalStrength
members.comment:
The current signal strength of the remote device.

 The resulting value can be  between `0.0` (weakest) and `1.0` (strongest), or it can be `nil` if the system can't measure the value.

members.name: transmitLatency
members.comment:
The measured transmit latency per access category that is in use with the remote devices and that the system can measure.

The system only reports in-use and measurable access categories. The dictionary is empty if there's no activity, or if the system can't measure the data.

members.name: throughputCeiling
members.comment:
The highest throughput the connection is capable of under ideal conditions, given the hardware capabilities of both devices.

The result is in `Mbps` and can be `nil` if the system can't calculate it.

members.name: throughputCapacity
members.comment:
The current estimated average throughput capacity of the data path, given the current radio conditions and concurrent Wi-Fi use cases.

The result is in `Mbps` and can be `nil` if the system can't calculate the capacity.

members.name: throughputCapacityRatio
members.comment:
The current normalized ratio of the throughput capacity and throughput ceiling.

This ratio reflects the current throughput capability of the data path as a value between `0.0` and `1.0`. It provides a consistent measure of the relative capacity and health of a data path, regardless of the different hardware capabilities across devices.

members.name: timestamp
members.comment: The time that the framework generates the report.

declarations.name: WAPerformanceReport.TransmitLatencyMetrics
declarations.comment: A report of the transmit latency to the specified peer.

members.name: accessCategory
members.comment: The Wi-Fi quality-of-service (QoS) category that this latency data tracks.

members.name: average
members.comment:
The average per-packet transmit latency measured for this flow's peers.

This property returns `nil` if the system can't measure the transmit latency.

declarations.name: WAPublishableService
declarations.comment:
A service, hosted by your app, that remote devices can connect to.

You specify the services your app uses in `Info.plist` via a dictionary under the <doc://com.apple.documentation/documentation/bundleresources/information-property-list/wifiawareservices> key:
- Each _key_ in that dictionary is the full service name of a service, and the _value_ is a dictionary of configuration properties for that service.
- If the configuration dictionary contains the `Publishable` key, the system creates a `WAPublishableService` is created for that service and makes it available in ``WAPublishableService/allServices``.

members.name: allServices
description
members.comment: A description of the service.

members.name: id
members.comment:
A stable ID that can be used to identify this publishable service.

The ID is stable for a given unique service name.

members.name: name
members.comment:
The full name of the service, as sent over the air.

To avoid conflicts with other apps and devices that may prevent your app from using
the service, register your service with a unique name in the
[IANA Service Name Registry](https://www.iana.org/assignments/service-names-port-numbers/service-names-port-numbers.xml).

For the service name to be valid, follow the rules located in [RFC 6763](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6763#section-4.1.2) and  [RFC 6335](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6335#section-5.1).

The RFC rules require that the service string have a unique name that conforms to the following rules:
* Only use characters such as `a-z`, `A-Z`, `0 - 9`, and hyphen (`-`).
* Use at least one letter `a-z`, `A-Z`.
* Don't start or end with a hyphen (`-`).
* Don't exceed 15 characters.

The full service name string then:

* Prepends an underscore (`_`) to the name component
* Adds a dot (`.`) separator
* Appends a protocol suffix of `_tcp` or `_udp`

The table below shows some examples:

Examples:
|  Name Component         |  Protocol Component |  Full Service Name string |
|-----------------------------|--------------------------|------------------------------------------|
| `example-service`  | `_tcp`                      | `_example-service._tcp`      |
| `example-service`  | `_udp`                      | `_example-service._udp`      |

The name in the `Info.plist` must be this full service name, exactly as it is sent over-the-air. Invalid service names in the `Info.plist` will cause the app to crash.

declarations.name: WAPublishableService.ID
declarations.comment: The type of value that uniquely identifies the service.

declarations.name: WAPublisherListener
declarations.comment:
Configures a network listener to publish a service over Wi-Fi Aware and accept incoming connections from paired devices.

Devices can publish services for other Wi-Fi Aware devices to use by creating a `NetworkListener` object from the
[Network](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/Network) framework, and passing in a `.wifiAware()` instruction indicating the
`WAPublishableService` to provide, and the set of `WAPairedDevice` that can connect to the service.
The code below configures the `NetworkListener` as a Wi-Fi Aware publisher by passing in a `.wifiAware()` instruction:
```swift
NetworkListener(for: .wifiAware( .connecting(to:service,  from:.selected(devices)) ) )
```

members.name: configureParameters
members.comment:
Configures the provided parameters for a Wi-Fi Aware publish operation and connection.
- Parameter parameters: The `NWParameters` to configure.

members.name: isApplicationService
members.comment:
A Boolean value that determines whether the devices are listening for an application service.

The value is `true` if a device is listening for an application service. The value is `false` otherwise.

members.name: service
members.comment: The service data for the Wi-Fi Aware publish operation.

declarations.name: WAPublisherListener.Action
declarations.comment:
The structure that configures the Wi-Fi Aware publisher operation that the network listener performs.

The configuration includes the service and devices it operates on.

The ``WAPublisherListener/Action`` is the first component of the `.wifiAware()` instruction to a `NetworkListener`.

The code below is an example of creating a `NetworkListener`:

```swift
NetworkListener(for: .wifiAware( .connecting(to:service,  from:.selected(devices)) ) )
````

members.name: connecting
members.signature: static func connecting(to myPublishingService: WAPublishableService, from pairedDevices: WAPublisherListener.Devices, datapath wifiAware: WAPublisherListener.DatapathParameters? = nil) -> WAPublisherListener.Action
members.comment:
Publishes the provided service over Wi-Fi, enabling connections from the specified paired devices.

When publishing, the `NetworkListener` provides a `NetworkConnection` object for each paired device that connects.

You can set the data path parameters, including the ``WAPerformanceMode``, in the optional "`datapath:`" parameter, or by using ``WAParameters`` that are written into the <doc://com.apple.documentation/documentation/Network/NWParameters> for the `NetworkListener`.

> Important: Each service must have the same ``WAPerformanceMode`` on both the `NetworkBrowser` (subscriber) and `NetworkListener` (publisher) sides of the connection, or the resulting performance behavior is undefined. If not specified, the performance mode defaults to ``WAPerformanceMode/bulk`` on both sides.
- Parameters:
  - myPublishingService: The service the publisher hosts, and accept connections to.
  - pairedDevices: The remote devices to accept connections from. The `NetworkListener` isn't activated if the system doesn't specify any devices.
  - wifiAware: The parameters specifying the initial Wi-Fi Aware data path configuration for any resulting connections, or `nil` to apply default parameters.
- Returns: A new `Action` configuring this operation.

members.name: addingConnections
members.signature: static func addingConnections(from pairedDevices: WAPublisherListener.Devices) -> WAPublisherListener.Action

declarations.name: WAPublisherListener.DatapathParameters
declarations.comment:
The parameter that sets the initial Wi-Fi Aware data path configuration for any devices that are connected.

The `DatapathParameters` is an optional "`datapath:`" component of the
`.wifiAware()` instruction to a `NetworkListener`. If you don't set a
specific parameter, then the system applies the default parameters with bulk
performance mode.

The code below is an example of how to set a data path configuration:

```swift
NetworkListener(for: .wifiAware( .connecting(to:service,  from:.selected(devices)) datapath: .defaults) )
```
> Important: Each service must have the same ``WAPerformanceMode`` on both the `NetworkBrowser` (subscriber) and `NetworkListener` (publisher) sides of the connection, or the resulting performance behavior is undefined. If not specified, the performance mode defaults to ``WAPerformanceMode/bulk`` on both sides.

members.name: defaults
members.comment:
The property that configures default parameters that prioritize bulk throughput, power consumption, and other concurrent Wi-Fi use cases.

- Returns: Default parameters.

members.name: realtime
members.comment:
Parameters that prioritize latency at the expense of throughput, power consumption, and other concurrent Wi-Fi use cases and devices.

- Returns: Realtime parameters.

declarations.name: WAPublisherListener.Devices
declarations.comment:
The structure that determines the devices to connect to.

This structure determines the devices the `NetworkListener` acts on or allows
connections from when publishing and includes only the devices that are relevant
for a given `NetworkListener` operation and use case. It allows your app to
include only the devices that are relevant for a given `NetworkListener`
operation and use case.

`Devices` is the "`from:`" component of the `.wifiAware()` instruction to a `NetworkListener`.

The code below is an example of configuring a `NetworkListener` with specific devices to allow connections from:

```swift
NetworkListener(for: .wifiAware( .connecting(to:service,  from:.selected(devices)) ) )
```

> Important: Only include the devices your app intends to use with the use case. Including unnecessary devices may impose additional power and performance costs on both the local and remote devices, and may reduce privacy.

members.name: userSpecifiedDevices
members.comment:
Includes only new devices the user pairs via DeviceDiscoveryUI's `DevicePairingView()`.

Only applicable to use with the `DevicePairingView()` API. Will throw an error if used with a `NetworkListener`.

members.name: allPairedDevices
members.comment: The property that includes all paired devices that your app has access to.

members.name: matching
members.signature: static func matching(_ pairedDevicesFilter: Predicate<WAPairedDevice>) -> WAPublisherListener.Devices
members.comment:
Includes only paired devices matching the provided live filter predicate.

- Parameter pairedDevicesFilter: The filter to apply to choose paired devices for this operation.
- Returns: A new `Devices` containing the device filter to use.

members.name: selected
members.signature: static func selected(_ pairedDevices: WAPairedDevice.Devices) -> WAPublisherListener.Devices
members.comment:
Includes only the preselected paired devices in the provided dictionary.
- Parameter pairedDevices: A ``WAPublisherListener/Devices`` dictionary holding a snapshot  of paired devices to use for this operation.

declarations.name: WAService
declarations.signature: protocol WAService : CustomStringConvertible, Decodable, Encodable, Hashable, Identifiable, Sendable
declarations.comment:
A protocol that defines a service that a device can publish or subscribe to.

A service represents a specific function or use case that's performed over Wi-Fi Aware. Services are specific functionality and protocols that your app can publish or subscribe to on other devices.

Services are identified by a service name string that follows the rules in [RFC 6763](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6763#section-4.1.2) and [RFC 6335](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6335#section-5.1). For a service name of `example-service`, the full service name encoded in the `Info.plist` and sent over the air is either `_example-service._tcp` if using the TCP protocol or `_example-service._udp` if using any other protocol.

You must register your app with a unique name in the [IANA service name registry](https://www.iana.org/assignments/service-names-port-numbers/service-names-port-numbers.xml) to avoid conflicts with other apps and devices.

If you have an invalid service name in the `Info.plist`, your app crashes.

declarations.name: WASharedSecret
declarations.comment:
A high-entropy shared secret unique to this network connection, which can be used to pair and setup security for higher layer network protocols like TLS, QUIC or IPSec without requiring manual action or data entry by a user.

The shared secret can be used to authenticate a [PAKE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Password-authenticated_key_agreement) like SPAKE2, which is then used to pair and derive long-term asymmetric keys for authentication and encryption of the upper-layer network protocol.

Both sides of a connection will derive the same shared secret value if the same connection and input parameters are used:
- Your app and a remote app can derive the same shared secret value by calling the ``WiFiAware/WAConnection/deriveSharedSecret(for:method:context:)`` function on the same connection, with the same parameters.
- Devices and accessories can derive the same value as your app by using the derivation specified in the Wi-Fi Aware 5.0 standard, and providing the same parameters as used by your app.

Example Usage to get a shared secret:
```swift
let secret = await connection.wifiAware?.deriveSharedSecret(for: .tlsPSK, method: .kdfHash256)
```

>Important: If needed, get a new shared secret for each new network connection. Do not save this value, send it to other devices, reuse it across connections, or use it as a long-term authentication or encryption key. Instead, use this to pair higher layer protocols, and derive unique longer-term asymmetric keys for those protocols when pairing them.

members.name: derivation
members.comment: The method used to derive the shared secret on both sides of the connection, as per the Wi-Fi Aware standard.

members.name: data
members.comment: The secret data that is derived by both this device and the remote device for this connection.

declarations.name: WASharedSecret.Context
declarations.comment: A unique value that is specific to your App and the use case a given connection will perform, which diversifies the generated secret so that it is unique to your App and connection.

members.name: bundleID
members.comment: Use your App's bundle ID as the context (default).

members.name: init
members.comment:
Create a new custom context, providing unique data for the context.

Custom context may use any data. The exact same byte value must be set on both the local and remote devices for the same shared secret to be generated.

- Parameter data: The data to use as the underlying context, which must be >= 3 bytes long.
- Returns: A new Context, or `nil` if the provided string was too short.

members.name: init
members.comment:
Create a new custom context, providing a unique string for the context.

Custom context may use any string that can be represented as UTF-8, and which normalizes to the same value when represented as bytes. ASCII-compatible values are recommended to avoid normalization issues. The exact same value must be set on both the local and remote devices for the same shared secret to be generated.

- Parameter string: The string to use as the underlying context, which must be >= 3 characters long. Will be converted to `UTF-8` prior to being hashed in the derivation.
- Returns: A new Context, or `nil` if the provided string was too short.

declarations.name: WASharedSecret.DerivationMethod
declarations.comment: An enumeration of methods that can be used to derive a shared secret, as specified in the Wi-Fi Aware standard.

members.name: kdfHash256
members.comment: Derive a shared secret using the KDF-HASH-256 method defined in the WiFi Aware 5.0 draft standard.

declarations.name: WASharedSecret.ProtocolName
declarations.comment: An object that uniquely identifies a particular network protocol and the pairing hanshake it uses for authentication.

members.name: tlsPSK
members.comment:
Derive a shared secret to bootstrap TLS, using the resulting shared secret as a TLS Pre-Shared Key.

Best practices for TLS security are described in [NIST Special Publication 800-52](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/52/r2/final). TLS 1.3 is recommended.

Specifying this value will use the "`TLS-PSK`" string as the protocol name when deriving the shared secret.

members.name: ipsecPSK
members.comment:
Derive a shared secret to bootstrap IPSec, using the resulting shared secret as the IPSec Pre-Shared Key.

Best practices for IPSec security are described in [NIST Special Publication 800-77](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/77/r1/final). IKEv2 and IPSec-v3 are recommended.

Specifying this value will use the "`IPSec-PSK`" string as the protocol name when deriving the shared secret.

members.name: init
members.comment:
Create a new custom protocol, providing a unique string for the context data.

Custom protocols should specify data that identifies the protocol that will use the shared secret. The exact same byte value must be set on both the local and remote devices for the same shared secret to be generated.

- Parameter data: The data to use as the underlying protocol name, which must be >= 3 bytes long.
- Returns: A new ProtocolName, or `nil` if the provided data was too short.

members.name: init
members.comment:
Create a new custom protocol name, providing a unique string for the protocol name.

Custom protocols should specify a string that identifies the protocol that will use the shared secret. The string must be representable as UTF-8, and normalize to the same value when represented as bytes. ASCII-compatible values are recommended to avoid normalization issues. The exact same value must be set on both the local and remote devices for the same shared secret to be generated.

- Parameter string: The string to use as the underlying protocol name, which must be >= 3 characters long. Will be converted to `UTF-8` prior to being hashed in the derivation.
- Returns: A new ProtocolName, or `nil` if the provided string was too short.

declarations.name: WASubscribableService
declarations.comment:
A service your app discovers on remote devices and can connect to.

You specify the services your app uses in `Info.plist` via a dictionary under the `WiFiAwareServices` key:
- Each _key_ in that dictionary is the full name of a service, and the _value_ is a dictionary of configuration properties for that service.
- If the configuration dictionary contains the `Subscribable` key, the system creates a `WASubscribableService`  for that service and makes it available in `WASubscribableService.allServices`.

members.name: allServices
description
members.comment: A string description of the service.

members.name: id
members.comment:
A stable ID that can be used to identify this subscribable service.

The ID is stable for a given unique service name.

members.name: name
members.comment:
The full name of the service, as sent over the air.

To avoid conflicts with other apps and devices that may prevent your app from using
the service, register your service with a unique name in the
[IANA Service Name Registry](https://www.iana.org/assignments/service-names-port-numbers/service-names-port-numbers.xml).

For the service name to be valid, follow the rules located in [RFC 6763](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6763#section-4.1.2) and  [RFC 6335](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6335#section-5.1).

The RFC rules require that the service string have a unique name that conforms to the following rules:
* Only use characters such as `a-z`, `A-Z`, `0 - 9`, and hyphen (`-`).
* Use at least one letter `a-z`, `A-Z`.
* Don't start or end with a hyphen (`-`).
* Don't exceed 15 characters.

The full service name string then:

* Prepends an underscore (`_`) to the name component
* Adds a dot (`.`) separator
* Appends a protocol suffix of `_tcp` or `_udp`

The table below shows some examples:

|  Name Component  |  Protocol Component |  Full Service Name string |
|---|---|---|
| `example-service` | `_tcp` | `_example-service._tcp` |
| `example-service` | `_udp` | `_example-service._udp` |

The name in the `Info.plist` must be this full service name, exactly as it's sent over the air. Invalid service names in the `Info.plist` cause the app to crash.

declarations.name: WASubscribableService.ID
declarations.comment: The type of value that uniquely identifies the service.

declarations.name: WASubscriberBrowser
declarations.comment:
The structure that configures a network browser to subscribe to a Wi-Fi Aware service and make outgoing connections to paired devices.

Devices can subscribe to services provided by other Wi-Fi Aware devices by creating a `NetworkBrowser` object from the
[Network](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/Network) framework, and passing in a `.wifiAware()` instruction indicating the
`WASubscribableService` to look for, and the set of `WAPairedDevice` to find it on.

The code below configures the `NetworkBrowser` as a Wi-Fi Aware subscriber by passing in a `.wifiAware()` instruction:
```swift
NetworkBrowser(for: .wifiAware( .connecting(to:.selected(devices),  from:service) ) )
```

members.name: makeEndpoint
members.signature: func makeEndpoint(from browseResult: NWBrowser.Result) throws -> WASubscriberBrowser.Endpoint?
members.comment:
Creates a connectable Wi-Fi Aware endpoint from a browse result.
- Parameter browseResult: The result of the `NWBrowser` operation.
- Returns: A `WAEndpoint` that you can connect to, or `nil` if it can't be created.
- Throws: An error if the result isn't valid.

members.name: makeDescriptor
members.comment:
Makes a descriptor that can create a network browser for a Wi-Fi Aware subscribe operation.

- Returns: A new `Descriptor`  that configures the `NetworkBrowser` for Wi-Fi Aware.

members.name: configureParameters
members.comment:
Returns the parameters to use to configure the Wi-Fi Aware subscriber and the subsequent connection.
- Parameter parameters: The parameters to use to configure the subscriber.
- Returns: A new `NWParameters`, updated to include the Wi-Fi Aware parameters.

declarations.name: WASubscriberBrowser.Action
declarations.comment:
The structure that configures the Wi-Fi Aware subscriber operation the network browser performs.

The configuration includes the service and devices it operates on.

The ``WASubscriberBrowser/Action`` is the first component of the `.wifiAware()` instruction to a `NetworkBrowser`.

The code below is an example of creating a `NetworkBrowser`:
```swift
NetworkBrowser(for: .wifiAware( .connecting(to:.selected(devices),  from:service) ) )
```

members.name: connecting
members.signature: static func connecting(to pairedDevices: WASubscriberBrowser.Devices, from mySubscribingService: WASubscribableService) -> WASubscriberBrowser.Action
members.comment:
Subscribes to the provided service over Wi-Fi, providing browse results for connecting to the specified paired devices if available.

When subscribing, the `NetworkBrowser` provides a ``WAEndpoint`` for each discovered paired device, and the app can then create a `NetworkConnection` object to connect to each. Data path parameters including the ``WAPerformanceMode`` are set when creating the connection, using ``WAParameters`` written into the <doc://com.apple.documentation/documentation/Network/NWParameters> for the `NetworkConnection`.

- Parameters:
  - pairedDevices: The devices to connect to. The browser isn't activated if no devices are specified.
  - mySubscribingService: The service to discover.
- Returns: A new `Action` configuring this operation.

declarations.name: WASubscriberBrowser.Devices
declarations.comment:
The structure that determines the devices to connect to.

This structure determines the devices the `NetworkBrowser` acts on when subscribing, such as which devices to try to connect to.
It allows your app to include only the devices that are relevant for a given `NetworkBrowser` operation and use case.

`Devices` is the `to:` component of the `.wifiAware()` instruction to a `NetworkBrowser`.

The code below is an example of configuring a `NetworkBrowser` with specific devices to connect to:
```swift
NetworkBrowser(for: .wifiAware( .connecting(to:.selected(devices),  from:service) ) )
```

> Important: Only include the devices your app intends to use with the use case. Including unnecessary devices may impose additional power and performance costs on both the local and remote devices, and may reduce privacy.

members.name: userSpecifiedDevices
members.comment:
Includes only devices the user selects or pairs in DeviceDiscoveryUI's `DevicePicker()`.

Only applicable to use with the `DevicePicker()` API. Will throw an error if used with a `NetworkBrowser`.

members.name: allPairedDevices
members.comment: The property that includes all paired devices that your app has access to.

members.name: matching
members.signature: static func matching(_ pairedDevicesFilter: Predicate<WAPairedDevice>) -> WASubscriberBrowser.Devices
members.comment:
Includes only paired devices matching the provided live filter predicate.
- Parameter pairedDevicesFilter: The filter to apply to choose paired devices for this operation.
- Returns: A new `Devices` containing the device filter to use.

members.name: selected
members.signature: static func selected(_ pairedDevices: WAPairedDevice.Devices) -> WASubscriberBrowser.Devices
members.comment:
Includes only the preselected paired devices in the provided dictionary.
- Parameter pairedDevices: A ``Devices`` dictionary holding a snapshot  of paired devices to use for this operation.
- Returns: A new ``WASubscriber/Devices`` including the selected devices.

globals.name: wifiAware
globals.comment:
Get an `WAEndpoint` that can connect to this `NWEndpoint`'s remote device over Wi-Fi Aware on the specified port, or `nil` if the `NWEndpoint` is not compatible with Wi-Fi Aware.

The returned endpoint can be used to connect to a remote `NetworkListener` that accepts additional Wi-Fi Aware connections without publishing a service, via  ``WiFiAware/WAPublisherListener/Action/addingConnections(from:)``

The returned endpoint will use Wi-Fi Aware as a transport.

- Returns: A new endpoint that can be used to connect over Wi-Fi Aware, or `nil` if it not compatible with Wi-Fi Aware.
